Case: Hector is a 55-year-old presenting with 9 months of progressive low-back and leg pain. Hector states that his pain is worse after prolonged ambulation and radiates to his right buttock and thigh. Hector has tried physical therapy and conservative pain medications including epidural steroid injections and NSAIDs. On physical exam, you observe that his pain is significantly worse with a right straight-leg raise and there are no focal deficits. Flexion-extension X rays show dynamic instability of L4 on L5.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Hector? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
